title: Hit-conditioned A/B replay harness with perturbation matrix
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a reproducible A/B replay harness that isolates requests by KV/prefix cache hit status and systematically measures semantic deltas induced by cache hits across model/config changes. This ticket implements a perturbation matrix for small prompt variants, a token-aligned diff scorer, and automated gating rules used by canaries and rollouts. The goal is to detect subtle output drift caused by caching semantics before a rollout affects customer traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a 50k request sample stratified into 'cold', 'warm-hit', 'partial-hit' and 'miss' buckets
Token-aligned diff scorer computed for each pair and produces an artefact with per-request edit-distance, ngram-overlap, and embedding-similarity metrics
Perturbation matrix (10 variants per request: punctuation, trailing space, newline, short suffix, prefix rephrase) executes and reports sensitivity per-bucket
Automated canary policy triggers when semantic-delta threshold exceeded (default: embedding-similarity drop > 0.06 and median edit-distance increase > 3 tokens for warm-hit bucket)
Results stored in runtime-evals S3 prefix and surfaced in a console dashboard with per-model, per-config breakdown
design_notes: We will implement a lightweight replay agent that pulls recent traffic samples from the golden-requests store and replays them deterministically through two runtime variants: baseline (no-cache or previous runtime config) vs candidate (with changed cache/config).

Token alignment: use the existing tokenization service to align output tokens and compute a weighted edit-distance where substitutions at earlier tokens and at punctuation carry higher weight to catch truncation/regeneration issues.

Perturbation matrix rationale: many cache-related regressions only surface with tiny prompt shifts; systematic perturbations increase sensitivity without bloating dataset. Variants chosen to reflect realistic client noise patterns.

Bucket logic: treat responses as 'hit' if KV-proxy returns HCID signature and duration < X ms; 'partial-hit' when KV produced prefix but model generated rest; we will reuse signal instrumentation from ENG-24890.
Performance: replay should support 100 rps distributed across workers; scoring runs asynchronously and writes per-request metrics to evaluation artifacts for later aggregation.
rollout_plan: Run the harness in shadow mode on nightly snapshots for every proposed cache/config change
If warm-hit bucket median semantic-delta exceeds threshold, fail canary and create automated rollback recommendation
For low-severity deltas, surface nightly digest to PM/QA for triage; for high-severity, block rollout and open ENG rollback runbook
Integrate gating with console rollout UI so operators see a red/yellow/green signal tied to this evaluation
tests: Unit: token alignment module tests with synthetic insert/delete/substitute cases
Integration: end-to-end replay against a local runtime pair (baseline vs candidate) with synthetic golden set
Regression: run harness against historical model-change commits where known cache regressions occurred to validate sensitivity
Canary: execute on a small live-sampled dataset (1%) with throttled concurrency before enabling full canary
